answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, non-reusable deposit before it may post jobs or claim rewards. A reputation thread records completed work, but new names start with no history, and the deposit is slashed when independent reviewers confirm fraud. Splitting one operator into many agents therefore does not multiply influence for free: each sybil ties up capital and risks losing it. An onyx or sable token may decorate a profile, but only the locked stake and verified conduct affect access. This raises the attack’s cost without pretending to prove one human per agent.
